summary.text: Andre Easton, a lifelong Bronx resident and public-school teacher who ran on the Party for Socialism and Liberation line in his first political campaign, lost the November 3, 2026 election for U.S. House in New York's 15th Congressional District to Ritchie Torres.
He completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey, describing a platform built around public housing, a $30 minimum wage, and ending U.S. military aid to Israel.

paragraphs.text: In a Ballotpedia survey response, Easton describes himself as "an educator, father, husband, and socialist" and a lifelong Bronx resident.

According to the Bronx Times, he has taught in South Bronx public schools since 2012 and describes the work as 14 years as a South Bronx educator, while his own survey response gives 13 years of teaching English there; the paper calls him a high school teacher.

His 2026 run was his first political campaign, per the Bronx Times; he is a member of the Party for Socialism and Liberation, which ran him as an independent candidate, and he hosted a series of campaign events called "Class is in Session" on Bronx issues.
He received 8.7% of the vote to Ritchie Torres's 76.8%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
